sentences.text: At the very outset, learned counsel for the applicant states that the purpose of the applicant would suffice if an order is passed directing the trial court to decide the bail application of the applicant, as expeditiously as possible.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 20 January, 2023.json

sentences.text: He further states that although the prayer has been made for quashing of the charge sheet, cognizance order and the entire proceedings of the case but he does not press the same.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 20 January, 2023.json

sentences.text: He further states that the applicant shall raise all the questions before the trial court.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 20 January, 2023.json

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the State has no objection of aforesaid arguments of learned counsel for the applicant.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 20 January, 2023.json

sentences.text: In view of the above, the prayer for quashing of proceedings/cognizance order/charge sheet is dismissed as not pressed.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 20 January, 2023.json

sentences.text: However, in view of the peculiar facts and circumstances of the case and looking to the limited prayer of learned counsel for the applicant, it is directed that if the accused-applicant surrenders before the trial court and applies for bail within two weeks from today, the same shall be considered and decided expeditiously in accordance with law.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 20 January, 2023.json

sentences.text: Till the aforesaid period, no coercive action shall be taken against the applicant.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 20 January, 2023.json

sentences.text: It it clarified that if the accused-applicant does not appear before the court concerned by the said date, the court concerned shall proceed against him in accordance with law.

sentences.text: The present application is disposed of.

Record shows that, in respect of an incident which is alleged to have occurred on 2.5.2022, a belated F.I.R. dated 5.5.2022 was lodged by first informant- Sanjo Devi and was registered as Case Crime No. 73 of 2022, under Sections 363, 366, 323, 354-B IPC and Section 376-D IPC and Section 5g, 6,
7, 8 POCSO Act, Police Station- Vichawan, District Mainpuri.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: In the aforesaid F.I.R. three persons namely, Ravi, Sunil and Sanjay have been nominated as named accused.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: The gravamen of the allegations made in the F.I.R. is to the effect that named accused enticed away the minor daughter of first informant namely, X aged about 16 years.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: After aforementioned F.I.R. was lodged, Investigating Officer proceeded with statutory investigation of concerned case crime number in terms Chapter XII Cr.P.C.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: The prosecutrix was recovered on 9.5.2023.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: Thereafter the statement of the prosecutrix was recorded under section 161 Cr.P.C., Same is on record at page 26 of the paper book.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: The prosecutrix in her aforesaid statement has supported the F.I.R. and has established the complicity of named accused and two other accused.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: However, in her aforesaid statement she has not alleged that her modesty was dislodged by any of the accused.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: Thereafter the prosecutrix was requested for her medical examination.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: The prosecutrix in her statement before the Doctor who medically examined her has rejoined her earlier statement recorded under section 161 Cr.P.C.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: The Doctor who examined the prosecutrix, however, did not find any signs on her body so as to denote commission of sexual assault.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text:
With reference to private part of the prosecutrix, the Doctor opined as follows:-
"Hymen- Intact"
sentences._hearing_file: Sunil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: Ultimately, the statement of the prosecutrix was recorded under section 164 Cr.P.C. which is on record at page 46 of the paper book.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: However, the prosecutrix in her aforesaid statement has departed from her earlier statement recorded under section 161 Cr.P.C. and before the Doctor.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: During course of investigation, Investigating Officer recovered the Transfer certificate of the prosecutrix.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: In the said copy of the Scholar Register/certificate the date of birth of the prosecutrix is recorded as 1.1.2006.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: The occurrence is alleged to have occurred on 2.5.2022.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: As such, the prosecutrix was aged about 16 years and four months.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: Investigating Officer also examined first informant and other witnesses under section 161 Cr.P.C who have substantially supported the F.I.R.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: On the basis of above and other material collected by Investigating Officer, during course of investigation he came to the conclusion that complicity of applicant is established in the crime in question.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: He, accordingly submitted the charge sheet dated 5.9.2022, whereby all the named accused have been charge sheeted under sections 363, 366, 323, 354-B IPC and Section 376-D IPC and Section 5g, 6, 7, 8 POCSO Act, Police Station- Vichawan, District Mainpuri.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: Learned counsel for applicant submits that this Court passed an order dated 17.7.2023, whereby CJM Mainpuri was directed to get the ossification test of the prosecutrix conducted.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text:
For ready reference the order dated 17.7.2023 is reproduced herein under:
"Heard Sri Sumit Kumar Srivastava, learned counsel for the applicant, learned AGA for the State and perused the record.

sentences.text:
By means of the present bail application, the applicant is involved in case crime no.
73 of 2022 under Sections 363, 366, 323, 354B, 376D IPC and Sections 5g, 6, 7,8 of the POCSO Act, P.S. Vichawan, District Mainpuri.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: Submission made by the counsel that as per the FIR the age of the girl is 16 years and 4 months as per her Transfer Certificate.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: There is nothing on record to establish the age of the victim on the date of the incident.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: Under such circumstances, CJM, Mainpuri and CMO, Mainpuri are directed to organize the ossification test of the victim.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: CMO, Mainpuri is required to constitute a panel of three senior doctors, who shall conduct the ossification test of the victim and give opinion about the expected age of the victim on the date of the incident to be disclosed by the victim or the informant of the case.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: This exercise has to be completed within a period of 15 days and CJM, Mainpuri shall ensure the presence of victim before the panel of doctor and give its report in a sealed cover on or before 08.08.2023 before this Court.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: Put up this case as fresh on 08.08.2023 before appropriate Court.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: Let copy of this order may be given to learned AGA for communication and compliance of the order. "
sentences._hearing_file: Sunil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: In compliance of above order dated 17.7.2023, CJM, Mainpuri has submitted his report, annexeing alongwith the same, the report of the medical board.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: As per the medical opinion the prosecutrix is said to be aged about 17 years.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: Learned counsel for applicant contends that though the applicant is a named and charge sheeted accused but he is innocent.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: Applicant has been falsely implicated in above mentioned case crime number.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: Referring to the statements of the prosecutrix recorded under section 161 Cr.P.C. before the Doctor and under section 164 Cr.P.C. he submits that prosecutrix has departed from her earlier statement in his subsequent statement recorded under section 164 Cr.P.C.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: At this juncture, learned counsel for applicant has invited the attention of Court to the judgment of Supreme Court in Phool Singh Vs. State of M.P. (2022) 2 SCC 74 and on basis thereof, he submits that prosecution of an accused for an offense of rape or sexual assault can be maintained even in the absence of medical evidence and on the solitary statement of prosecutrix.

entities.text: Phool Singh Vs. State of M.P. (2022) 2 SCC 74
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences._hearing_file: Sunil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: However, in such a circumstance, the statement of the prosecutrix must be clear, categorical and consistent.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: The same should also be devoid of any ambiguity.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: Meaning thereby it should be of impeccable character.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: When the statement of the prosecutrix is examined in the light of above, it cannot be said that the same is of impeccable character.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: No prosecution of applicant can be maintained on the basis of said statement of the prosecutrix.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text:
Co-accused Sanjay has already been enlarged on bail by this Court vide Sunil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 17 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163243959/
3 order dated 1.6.2023, passed in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 6771 of 2023 (Sanjay Vs. State of U.P.a nd three others).

sentences.text: Copy of which is on record at page 51 of the paper book.

sentences.text: On the above premise, it is urged by learned counsel for applicant that case of present applicant is similar and identical to aforementioned co-accused.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: There is no such distinguishing feature on the basis of which case of present applicant can be distinguished from aforesaid accused so as to deny him bail.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: He, therefore, submits that in view of above and for the facts and reasons recorded in the obove order, present applicant is also liable to be enlarged on bail.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: Even otherwise, applicant is a man of clean antecedents inasmuch as he has no criminal history to his credit except the present one.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: Applicant is in jail since 16.8.2022.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: As such, he has undergone more than ten months of incarceration.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: It is thus urged that applicant is liable to be enlarged on bail.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: In case the applicant is enlarged on bail, he shall not misuse the liberty of bail and shall co-operate with the trial.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: Per contra, the learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer for bail.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: He submits that since applicant is a named as well as charge sheeted accused, therefore he does not deserve any indulgence by this Court.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: However, he could not dislodge the factual and legal submissions urged by learned counsel for applicant, with reference to the record at this stage.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: Having heard the learned counsel for applicant, the learned A.G.A. for State, upon perusal of material brought on record, evidence, nature and gravity of offence as well as complicity of applicant, accusation made coupled with the fact that, when the statements of the prosecutrix when examined as a whole are not of impeccable character, the judgement of the Supreme Court in Phool Singh (Supra), the co-accused Sanjay has already been enlarged on bail, the learned A.G.A. could not point out from the record, that the case of present applicant is distinguishable from bailed out co-accused, the police report in terms of Section 173 (2) Cr.P.C. has already been submitted against applicant, as such, the entire evidence sought to be relied upon by prosecution against applicants stands crystalized, inspite of above, the learned A.G.A. could not point out any such circumstance from the record necessitating custodial arrest of applicant during pendency of trial, the judgementof the Supreme Court in Sumit Subhaschandra Gangwal and another Vs. The state of maharashtra and Another, 2023 Live law (SC) 373 (para 5) the period of incarceration undergone, the clean antecedents of applicant but without making any comment on the merits of the case, applicant has made out a case for bail.

opennyai_summary.17_August_2023__arguments:
At this juncture, learned counsel for applicant has invited the attention of Court to the judgment of Supreme Court in Phool Singh Vs. State of M.P. (2022) 2 SCC 74 and on basis thereof, he submits that prosecution of an accused for an offense of rape or sexual assault can be maintained even in the absence of medical evidence and on the solitary statement of prosecutrix.
However, in such a circumstance, the statement of the prosecutrix must be clear, categorical and consistent.
Having heard the learned counsel for applicant, the learned A.G.A. for State, upon perusal of material brought on record, evidence, nature and gravity of offence as well as complicity of applicant, accusation made coupled with the fact that, when the statements of the prosecutrix when examined as a whole are not of impeccable character, the judgement of the Supreme Court in Phool Singh (Supra), the co-accused Sanjay has already been enlarged on bail, the learned A.G.A. could not point out from the record, that the case of present applicant is distinguishable from bailed out co-accused, the police report in terms of Section 173 (2) Cr.P.C. has already been submitted against applicant, as such, the entire evidence sought to be relied upon by prosecution against applicants stands crystalized, inspite of above, the learned A.G.A. could not point out any such circumstance from the record necessitating custodial arrest of applicant during pendency of trial, the judgementof the Supreme Court in Sumit Subhaschandra Gangwal and another Vs. The state of maharashtra and Another, 2023 Live law (SC) 373 (para 5) the period of incarceration undergone, the clean antecedents of applicant but without making any comment on the merits of the case, applicant has made out a case for bail.
opennyai_summary.17_August_2023__ANALYSIS:
The same should also be devoid of any ambiguity.
Meaning thereby it should be of impeccable character.
When the statement of the prosecutrix is examined in the light of above, it cannot be said that the same is of impeccable character.
No prosecution of applicant can be maintained on the basis of said statement of the prosecutrix.
Co-accused Sanjay has already been enlarged on bail by this Court vide Sunil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 17 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163243959/
3 order dated 1.6.2023, passed in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 6771 of 2023 (Sanjay Vs. State of U.P.a nd three others).
There is no such distinguishing feature on the basis of which case of present applicant can be distinguished from aforesaid accused so as to deny him bail.
Even otherwise, applicant is a man of clean antecedents inasmuch as he has no criminal history to his credit except the present one.
Applicant is in jail since 16.8.2022.
As such, he has undergone more than ten months of incarceration.
opennyai_summary.17_August_2023__decision:
Accordingly, the bail application is Allowed.
Let the applicant Sunil, be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions which are being imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) THE APPLICANT SHALL FILE AN UNDERTAKING TO THE EFFECT THAT HE/SHE SHALL NOT SEEK ANY ADJOURNMENT ON THE DATE FIXED FOR EVIDENCE WHEN THE WITNESSES ARE PRESENT IN COURT.
IN CASE OF DEFAULT OF THIS CONDITION, IT SHALL BE OPEN FOR THE TRIAL COURT TO Sunil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 17 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163243959/
4 TREAT IT AS ABUSE OF LIBERTY OF BAIL AND PASS ORDERS IN ACCORDANCE WITH LAW.
(ii) THE APPLICANT SHALL REMAIN PRESENT BEFORE THE TRIAL COURT ON EACH DATE FIXED, EITHER PERSONALLY OR THROUGH HIS/HER COUNSEL.
IN CASE OF HIS/HER ABSENCE, WITHOUT SUFFICIENT CAUSE, THE TRIAL COURT MAY PROCEED AGAINST HIM/HER UNDER SECTION 229-A IPC.
(iii) IN CASE, THE APPLICANT MISUSES THE LIBERTY OF BAIL DURING TRIAL AND IN ORDER TO SECURE HIS/HER PRESENCE PROCLAMATION UNDER SECTION 82 CR.P.C., MAY BE ISSUED AND IF APPLICANT FAILS TO APPEAR BEFORE THE COURT ON THE DATE FIXED IN SUCH PROCLAMATION, THEN,
THE TRIAL COURT SHALL INITIATE PROCEEDINGS AGAINST HIM/HER, IN ACCORDANCE WITH LAW, UNDER SECTION 174-A IPC.
(iv) THE APPLICANT SHALL REMAIN PRESENT, IN PERSON, BEFORE THE TRIAL COURT ON DATES FIXED FOR (1) OPENING OF THE CASE, (2) FRAMING OF CHARGE AND (3) RECORDING OF STATEMENT UNDER SECTION 313 CR.P.C. IF IN THE OPINION OF THE TRIAL COURT ABSENCE OF THE APPLICANT IS DELIBERATE OR WITHOUT SUFFICIENT CAUSE, THEN IT SHALL BE OPEN FOR THE TRIAL COURT TO TREAT SUCH DEFAULT AS ABUSE OF LIBERTY OF BAIL AND PROCEED AGAINST THE HIM/HER IN ACCORDANCE WITH LAW.
(v) THE TRIAL COURT MAY MAKE ALL POSSIBLE EFFORTS/ENDEAVOUR AND TRY TO CONCLUDE THE TRIAL WITHIN A PERIOD OF ONE YEAR AFTER THE RELEASE OF THE APPLICANT.
However, it is made clear that any wilful violation of above conditions by the applicant, shall have serious repercussion on his/her bail so granted by this court and the trial court is at liberty to cancel the bail, after recording the reasons for doing so, in the given case of any of the condition mentioned above.
